answer: One concrete defense: gate each vote behind a verifiable delay function - a strictly sequential puzzle whose answer demands a fixed voyage of wall-clock time that no parallel silicon can shorten. A clone farm packed on a single mesa of servers cannot amortize it: ten thousand identities each grind the full elapsed computation, one narrow inlet at a time, since sequential steps refuse to run side by side. Forging a quorum thus costs real calendar time per fake instead of a cheap instant, and a vote-stuffing majority never arrives before the epoch closes.
